direction: Long-only failed-breakdown reclaim with a fixed five-day holding period
hypothesis: Some breaks below an established N-day low may reverse within the next K closes; entering only after a completed close reclaims the broken level may capture rebounds without buying the initial breakdown. This is a predeclared countertrend hypothesis, not a claim of an exact reproduction of the published Turtle Soup setup.

literature_context.source: Linda Bradford Raschke official recommended-reading list, which lists Street Smarts coauthored with Laurence A. Connors
literature_context.scope: Bibliographic origin context only; the evaluated rule below is our explicitly fixed long-only daily adaptation, not the authors’ complete setup or proof of crypto profitability.
Secondary historical description of fading failed channel breaks; used only to motivate the idea, not as performance evidence.

This grid changes the event to a one-shot close reclaim of the specific level broken earlier; it remains related countertrend research and shares repeated historical selection risk.

data.exchange: Binance spot archived 1-minute OHLCV aggregated into continuous UTC daily OHLCV. Execution uses the exact following-day 00:01 1m open from the same real archived data; no earlier or later bar is selected.

rule.setup: At completed UTC daily close t, when flat and no setup is pending, arm a failed-breakdown setup only if close[t] is strictly below lower[t]=min(low[t-N:t]); the N prior completed daily bars exclude t. Store that exact lower level and expiry day index t+K.
rule.reclaim: On one of the next K completed daily closes after the breakdown day (inclusive of day t+K), if close[j] is strictly above the stored lower[t], enter long at the next UTC day 00:01 1-minute bar open. A reclaim on breakdown day itself is not allowed. While pending, ignore any subsequent new lows and retain the first broken level. If K days pass without reclaim, disarm after the expiry day close; a new breakdown may arm from the following closed day.
rule.hold_exit: Hold exactly H=5 elapsed UTC daily intervals from virtual entry timestamp; exit at the 00:01 UTC minute open after five full closed daily bars. Ignore all new breakdown/reclaim signals while holding and on the exit event day; setup processing resumes the next UTC daily decision. No stop, profit target or overlapping positions.
rule.sizing: One 2,000-USDT portfolio with separate BTC and ETH long-only cash sleeves; raw initial weights 0.50/0.50 (1,000 USDT each). Each signal uses its sleeve only; no cross-sleeve transfers/rebalancing, leverage, shorting or cash interest. Full available sleeve cash is allocated at entry; full units sold at exit.
rule.timing: Only fully closed UTC daily OHLC bars can arm, reclaim or exit. Daily close becomes available at next UTC 00:00; simulated order reference is the following 00:01 1-minute open, 60 seconds later. Warmup data may form the prior N-day levels, but there are no pre-OOS positions. OOS begins 2025-09-19 00:01 UTC and terminal liquidation is 2026-09-14 00:01 UTC.
rule.channel_extrema: Prior-low calculation excludes the compared day. Reclaim compares against the saved breakdown-day lower level, not a moving later channel.

grid.sensitivity: Full 3x3 grid over N-day prior-low setup lookback and K-day reclaim window; all combinations retained.

cost_model.impact: 0.5 * sample stdev of prior 20 fully closed daily log returns * sqrt(order quote budget / mean quote volume over prior 20 complete UTC days)

exchange_snapshot.percent_price_reference: Historical order filters use mean of prior five complete 1m closes as a proxy for the current avgPriceMins reference; exact historical exchange rule and book snapshots are unavailable.

benchmark_read_only.note: Read-only same 360-day start/end, separate 1,000-USDT BTC/ETH initial sleeves and cost scenes; do not recalculate this exact benchmark.
